title: logs_events — Iceberg table contract for the small-files scenario
description: Authoritative shape of the Iceberg table the seeder builds and the learner compacts. Schema and (lack of) partition spec are fixed: the project teaches file-layout maintenance, not partitioning. Partitioning was learned in iceberg-partitioning; here the table is intentionally UN-partitioned so the small-files problem cannot be masked by partition pruning.

columns.name: event_id
columns.description: Globally unique event id; primary key, never null. Densely packed integers within a micro-batch.

columns.name: tenant_id
columns.description: Tenant identifier, 1..10. Skewed distribution — tenant 1 produces ~40% of traffic. Sort-order target #1.

columns.name: event_time
columns.description: Event timestamp, microsecond precision, spread over one hour. Sort-order target #2 (within tenant).

columns.name: event_type
columns.description: One of: page_view, click, purchase, error, signup. Low cardinality.

columns.name: payload
columns.description: Short payload string (~30 bytes). Bulk of the row size — present so 600 micro-batches × ~30 rows actually weigh in the KB range each.

notes: DELIBERATELY UN-PARTITIONED. The catalog already has iceberg-partitioning for that conversation. Here we focus on file layout within a single (unpartitioned) namespace.

The 'sort_order_target' is not enforced at table-creation time on purpose — the learner sets it via Table.replace_sort_order(...) (or via rewrite_data_files's sort strategy) as part of the compaction work.
The table identifier in the REST catalog is `default.logs_events`.
